[[File:Richard Parker, Mathematician, 2021.jpg|thumb|283x283px|Richard A. Parker]]
'''Richard A. Parker''' (29 January 1953 – 26 January 2024<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.richardparker.net/|title=Richard Parker Memorial|access-date=2024-02-05}}</ref>) was a mathematician and freelance computer programmer born in [[Surrey]] who lived for much of his life in [[Cambridge]], [[England]]. He invented many of the algorithms for computing the modular character tables  of finite [[simple group]]s. He discovered the relation between [[Niemeier lattice]]s and
deep holes of the [[Leech lattice]], and  constructed Parker's [[Moufang loop]] of order 2<sup>13</sup><ref name="Wilson2009">{{cite book|last=Wilson|first=Robert|title=The Finite Simple Groups|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lYMAg_Sj7hUC&pg=PA247|access-date=5 August 2012|year=2009|publisher=Springer|isbn=9781848009875|page=247}}</ref> (which was used by [[John Horton Conway]] in his construction of the [[monster group]]).
